newsitem.title: NEPAL: U.S. gives Nepal $30 mln grant for family planning.
newsitem.headline: U.S. gives Nepal $30 mln grant for family planning.

text.p: The United States is giving a 1.7-billion-rupee ($30 million) grant to Nepal to implement a family planning and maternal and child care programme, officials said on Thursday.

Officials said the money would be used by the poor Himalayan nation to reduce fertility rates, improve healthcare for mothers and children, and build skills among medical attendants to ensure safe childbirths.
A Finance Ministry statement said the U.S. grant aimed to reduce Nepal's total fertility rate from 4.6 at present to 4.0 by 2002.
The rate refers to the number of children a woman could give birth to if she lived through her child-bearing years.
The programme also intends to bring down the mortality rate of children under the age of five from 118 per thousand live births at present to 85.
"It is an ambitious project but I am sure we can achieve the goals," Sandy Vogelgesang, U.S. ambassador to Nepal, said after signing an agreement for the assistance on Thursday.
